get.summary: List alerts
get.description:
An alert denotes the sighting of one or more indicator given a set of events.
This paginated endpoint list all the alerts. A set of filters can be
specified to focus on certain alerts.

The following permissions are required:
 - “View alerts” (`9ea2b8a3-593f-4bab-92f5-d0af9b563f6f`)

patch.summary: Update the legacy status on a list of alerts
patch.description:
The list of selected alerts, on which the action will be performed,
is specified with the filter (url parameter)
`match[uuid]`, that accept a list of identifiers (or short_id) of alerts separated by commas, while the
identifier of the action is set in the body of the request as a json dictionary.

The identifier of the action is brought from the workflow (GET request on this endpoint).

The following permissions are required:
 - “Update alert status” (`9f3df1b1-4db7-44bd-b615-af5873ad7f8a`)

match[uuid].description: Match alerts by their identifier (uuid or short_id; separated by commas).

comment.description: A comment to describe why the alert status has changed

get.summary: List Cyber Kill Chain Stages
get.description:
The cyber kill chain (developed by Lockheed Martin) is an industry-accepted framework to
 describe and model the stages of an offensive cyber activity. An effective understanding of
the cyber kill chain greatly assists the information security professional in
 establishing the adversary’s tactics, techniques and procedures (TTPs).

The cyber kill chain is denoted by 7 steps:
1. Reconnaissance: Intruder selects target, researches it, and attempts to identify
 vulnerabilities in the target network.
2. Weaponization: Intruder creates remote access malware weapon, such as a virus or
 worm, tailored to one or more vulnerabilities.
3. Delivery: Intruder transmits weapon to target (e.g., via e-mail attachments,
 websites or USB drives).
4. Exploitation: Malware weapon's program code triggers, which takes action
 on target network to exploit vulnerability.
5. Installation: Malware weapon installs access point (e.g., "backdoor") usable by intruder.
6. Command and Control: Malware enables intruder to have "hands on the
 keyboard" persistent access to target network.
7. Actions on Objective: Intruder takes action to achieve their goals,
 such as data exfiltration, data destruction, or encryption for ransom.

This endpoint can be use to retrieve the different stages of the Cyber Kill Chain.

A stage is denoted by its unique identifier (`uuid`), its `name` and `description`.
In addition, every stage can be refered to by its `short_id`.

For example, the following denotes the **Reconnaissance** stage:
```
{
    'uuid': '73708d4f-419f-44aa-b505-288b522f9c30',
    'name': 'Reconnaissance',
    'description': 'Intruder selects target, researches it, and attempts to identify vulnerabilities.',
    'short_id': 'KCXKNfnJupq5'
}
```

The following permissions are required:
 - “View alerts” (`9ea2b8a3-593f-4bab-92f5-d0af9b563f6f`)

get.summary: Get the average time to close of the alerts
get.description:
The time to close is the time between the creation of an alert and its closure.
Alerts are selected and binned by their closure date: an alert counts in the period
during which it was closed, whenever it was created.

By default the response only holds the `all` group, covering every alert. With the
`with_elevate_split` parameter, the alerts are also split in two extra groups: the ones
investigated by Elevate (a verdict was set by the AI analyst) and the ones without
Elevate involvement.

For each group, this endpoint returns the average time to close over the requested period,
its trend (percent change vs the period of the same duration preceding it) and a
time-binned series (see the `precision` parameter).

With `group_by=community`, the response also holds a `communities` list carrying the
same groups per requested community.

The requested period is bound to 12 months and must be specified with the `date[closed_at]` parameter.

The following permissions are required:
 - “Read AI analytics” (`0175349f-7764-4287-8b5a-7cb045730472`)
 - “View alert statistics” (`b1642ef8-4bc0-40b4-9ddf-7bd368659941`)
